# EcoTrace datasets

Every dataset the EcoTrace app and its ML models use, exported from the project's MongoDB database (29 Oct 2026).

**The data is synthetic.** It's generated by `server/src/seed.js` for one demo company (Sahyadri Auto Components Pvt Ltd, Pune) and models realistic Indian freight patterns. It is not real company data. Emission factors approximate the UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for freighting goods.

## Files

| File | Rows | What it is | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shipments.csv` | 4,878 | Every shipment, Oct 2024 to Oct 2026: route, mode, weight, distance, CO2, cost, expected and actual days, delay flag, delay-risk score, anomaly flag | Dashboard, reports, all ML models |
| `ml_training_table.csv` | 4,878 | The same shipments in the exact form the ML service trains on (`load_shipments()` + `add_time_features()` in `ml/app/data.py`), with the engineered features | Delay-risk model, forecast, anomaly detection |
| `shipments_dataset.csv` | 4,878 | Earlier export of the same shipments (23 Oct 2026) in a compact snake_case format; a few statuses have changed since, so `shipments.csv` is the current version | Reference copy |
| `vendors.csv` | 11 | Suppliers: city, coordinates, materials, price per kg, monthly capacity, cluster label | Vendors page, optimizer, vendor clustering |
| `locations.csv` | 10 | Factory, warehouses and customer sites with coordinates | Shipments, route map, optimizer |
| `emission_factors.csv` | 4 | kg CO2e per tonne-km, cost per tonne-km, minimum charge, speed and handling days for road, rail, sea and air | CO2 and cost calculation |
| `cities.csv` | 49 | Built-in table of Indian cities (coordinates, coastal port yes/no), used for geocoding without an API key | Geocoding, sea-route availability |
| `distance_cache.csv` | 35 | Cached route distances between coordinate pairs | Routing |
| `co2_forecast_monthly.csv` | 27 | Monthly CO2: 24 months of actual history plus the SARIMA forecast with lower and upper bounds | Insights page |
| `companies.csv` | 1 | Company profile and monthly CO2 budget | Budget alerts |
| `users.csv` | 3 | Demo accounts and roles (no passwords) | Sign-in |
| `alerts.csv` | 1 | Alerts raised by the app | Alerts panel |
| `model_metrics.json` | | Scores of the trained models on held-out data | Insights page |

## Shipments at a glance

- Mode: road 4,114 · rail 600 · air 147 · sea 17
- Direction: inbound 2,712 · outbound 2,166
- Status: delivered 4,823 · in transit 55
- Delivered late: 27.3%
- Total CO2: about 3,386 tonnes
- 14 records are deliberately wrong (invoiced cost far from the tariff) so the anomaly detector has something to find; they have `anomaly.flag = true`.

## Built-in patterns

These were put into the data on purpose, so the models have real signals to learn:

- Monsoon (June to September) delays, strongest for road
- Festival-season volume peaks (September to November)
- Steady growth over the two years
- A few vendors that are often late

## Key columns

- `co2Kg` = `distanceKm` × (`weightKg` / 1000) × `emissionFactor`
- `delayed` is true when `actualDays` > `expectedDays`; it is the delay model's target.
- `ml_training_table.csv` features: `month`, `is_monsoon`, `is_festival`, `log_weight`, `inbound`, and one-hot `mode_road`, `mode_rail`, `mode_sea`, `mode_air`.

## Model results (`model_metrics.json`)

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| Delay risk: Random Forest (selected) | F1 0.564, ROC-AUC 0.761 on 965 held-out shipments |
| Delay risk: rule baseline (road + monsoon = late) | F1 0.535, ROC-AUC 0.680 |
| CO2 forecast: SARIMA | MAPE 7.97% vs 12.21% for "same as last month" |
| Anomaly detection: Isolation Forest | finds all 14 corrupted records |

## Recreating the data

- `cd server && npm run seed` regenerates the demo company in the database (this replaces its current data).
- `cd ml && .venv/bin/python scripts/generate_synthetic.py` writes a similar synthetic dataset in the CSV import format.
